title: The Owl and other strigiform nebulae: multipolar cavities within a filled shell

evidence.locator: Sect. 1: an inner shell of radius about 70 arcsec, most prominent in high-ionization lines, and a fainter outer shell of radius about 100 arcsec, most prominent in low-ionization lines; densities of about 50 and 30 per cubic cm times the same power of the filling factor. Sect. 2.3: the blue-shifted velocity channels show cavities on both sides of the central star, north-west and south-east, the red-shifted channels a single cavity on the south-east side, so at least three cavity lobes are required: one to the north-west pointing toward us, and two to the south-east, the more easterly toward us and the more southerly away. Sect. 3: a simple shell model was unsuitable; the H-alpha outline is modelled as a slightly prolate spheroid filled with uniform emission, the ratio of its axes about 1.13, at a position angle of about 60 degrees and an inclination of about 25 degrees with the north-west half pointing toward Earth; the multipolar cavity is a volume that multiplies the emission inside it by 0.3.
